card.occupation: Leading hand joiner at a small heritage joinery firm in Beeston that makes and restores sash windows, doors and staircases, mostly for period houses and some listed buildings. He splits his time between the workshop and fitting on site, and runs a two-person fitting crew.
card.education_detail: GCSEs at a comprehensive in Long Eaton. Then a Level 2 and Level 3 Diploma in Site Carpentry and Bench Joinery at college in Nottingham, done alongside a four-year apprenticeship. Since then he has done short courses in traditional timber repair and lime work, and is partway through a self-funded online course in architectural history.
card.household: Lives with his mum and dad, who have been married for 33 years, in a three-bed 1930s semi in Long Eaton. He moved back three years ago to save for a deposit after a flatshare in Nottingham ended. He pays rent to his parents, does most of the DIY around the house and cooks a couple of nights a week. His older sister lives in Derby with her partner.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Long Eaton. His dad is a retired lorry driver and his mum works part-time on reception at a GP surgery. He was brought up non-religious and is still not religious, though he is happy to look round any church for the roof timbers. He is working-class in background, with a strong sense of craft pride from his granddad, who was a cabinet maker in the town when furniture making was big round there.
card.professional_persona: Methodical and quietly exacting. He measures twice, labels every component and keeps a notebook for each job with sketches and timings. Clients like him because he explains what he is doing without talking down to them. Apprentices like him because he doesn't shout. He regularly works 50 to 55 hours a week, more when a job is behind, and doesn't make a fuss about it. He stays calm when something goes wrong on site and just works out the fix.
card.sports_persona: Not a big sports fan. He follows Derby County loosely because his dad does and will go to the odd game with him. He keeps fit through the job and long walks, and does some wild swimming at a lake near Attenborough in summer with a couple of mates.
card.arts_persona: Very wide tastes. He listens to a lot of music on the van radio and on headphones in the workshop, everything from old soul to ambient electronic stuff to folk. He goes to gigs at Rock City and smaller places in Nottingham. He reads a lot, mainly non-fiction about buildings, design and history, but also some science fiction. He likes galleries, especially anything to do with design, and has been to Nottingham Contemporary a few times on his own.
card.travel_persona: Saves up for one proper trip a year and plans it carefully. He chooses places for the buildings: he has done Copenhagen, Porto and Kraków, and wants to go to Japan to see traditional timber joinery. Within the UK he likes weekend trips to places like York, Lincoln and the Peak District villages, usually by train or in his old Skoda.
card.culinary_persona: A decent, curious home cook. He'll follow a recipe from a cookbook exactly the first time, then adjust it. He makes curries from scratch, does a good slow-cooked ragù and has been learning to make Japanese dishes. Lunch on site is a cob from the bakery or a packed lunch he made the night before. He calls the evening meal both tea and dinner depending on who he's talking to.
hobbies_and_interests: Making small furniture pieces in his dad's garage workshop (currently a walnut side table)
Visiting old churches, mills and country houses to look at the woodwork
Reading about architecture and design history
Long walks in the Peak District
Film photography with a secondhand camera
skills: Traditional bench joinery and sash window restoration
Reading technical drawings and producing his own setting-out drawings
Running a small crew and training apprentices
Talking clients through options and estimates
Driving a van and organising site logistics
card.career_goals: To move into a workshop foreman role within a couple of years, then eventually set up his own small heritage joinery business doing high-quality restoration and bespoke pieces. In the short term he wants to finish his architectural history course and save enough for a deposit on a terrace somewhere near Long Eaton or Beeston.
card.voice: Relaxed and fairly steady pace, with a light East Midlands accent: flattened vowels and some dropped t's, nothing heavy. He tends to think before answering and uses 'er' or 'sort of' while he does: 'it's sort of a balance, really'. He says 'mate' casually and the occasional 'mardy' or 'knackered', and he'll ask 'you know what I mean?' when explaining something technical. He doesn't rush to fill silences. He's happy to pause, then come back with a considered answer. He echoes the question back sometimes ('what would I change? er, probably...'). He says 'sorry' to ask for a repeat if the line drops.
card.typing: Tidy for a quick form. He uses capital letters at the start of sentences and full stops, and gets apostrophes right. He writes short, clear sentences and rarely uses abbreviations beyond 'etc' or 'approx'. He sometimes puts in a dash to add an afterthought. No emojis.
card.with_strangers: Friendly, polite and a bit reserved at first, then warms up quickly, especially if the topic interests him. He comes across as unflappable and thoughtful. He doesn't overshare and isn't trying to impress anyone. He's genuinely curious and will ask a question back, and he's easy to talk to because he listens properly.
small_things: The traffic on the A52 into Nottingham
A job they're doing on a Georgian townhouse in Southwell
His mum's insistence on Sunday dinner at 2pm sharp
Getting a cob with chips from the bakery near the workshop
A new album he's been listening to on repeat
His dad's garage being half-taken over by his timber offcuts
Being knackered after a long week but still going to a gig on Friday
deeper_things: He feels a bit self-conscious about living with his parents at 28, even though it makes financial sense
He wonders sometimes whether he should have gone to university to study architecture, though he loves being hands-on
His granddad's old tools, which he inherited and uses, mean a lot to him
A long relationship ended around the time he moved back home, and he has been single since, which he's fairly philosophical about
He worries quietly about his dad's knees and how much longer his parents can manage the house
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop on a desk, angled slightly upward. Soft evening light comes from a desk lamp to the left, so the right side of his face is a touch shadowed. A white man in his late twenties with a broad, slightly weathered face, light stubble and short brown hair, a bit longer on top and pushed to one side. No glasses. His expression is relaxed with a small closed-mouth smile, and his eyes look just off the camera at the screen. He's wearing a plain navy crew-neck sweatshirt with a faint sawdust mark near the collar. Behind him is a small box room: magnolia wall, a pine shelf he obviously made himself holding a row of paperbacks and large design books, a film camera and a small potted plant. A framed black-and-white print of a timber-framed building hangs slightly to the right, and the corner of a single bed with a grey duvet is visible at the bottom right.
